notes: Two of three pages were reachable. The NovaSeq 6000 downloads page lists NVCS v1.8.2 and a Software Suite Installer v1.8.2, both dated Aug 25, 2025. A search found no public release notes for v1.8.2 (only v1.8.0 and v1.8.1 notes), so its contents are unverified. The Clarity LIMS integration page (v3.2.1) carries no release dates and no mention of NovaSeq X. I did not reach the 6000Dx DRAGEN pages or a NovaSeq X cadence comparison. Neither page showed any end-of-support or 'last version' language. A 6000 control software release in Aug 2025 is the first in about 21 months, since v1.8.1 on Nov 6, 2023. That fits continued 6000 maintenance and no imminent end-of-life notice, but it is a weak signal. It could be a bug-fix or compatibility release. The page's date list conflicts with the search snippet, which shows v1.8.1 notes dated Mar/Oct 2023 (the page says Nov 6, 2023). The final 15K characters of the LIMS page were not read.
how_to_mine: 1) Open the v1.8.2 customer release notes PDF from the downloads page, to see whether it adds features, reagent support (e.g. 5B or other newer kits) or NovaSeq X compatibility, and whether it carries any 'end of support' language. 2) Fetch the same page with offset 100000 for the LIMS page tail. 3) Open the NovaSeq X Control Software downloads page and the 6000Dx / DRAGEN pages, and date their releases for comparison (X likely has several releases per year). 4) Check the Wayback Machine for the 6000 downloads page to see when v1.8.2 first appeared, and look for a v1.8.3 or v1.9 after Aug 2025.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Illumina shipped a new NovaSeq 6000 Control Software (v1.8.2) and Software Suite Installer on 25 Aug 2025, after the 6000 tail was in decline.
items.detail: The NovaSeq 6000 downloads page lists NVCS v1.8.2 and Installer v1.8.2 both dated Aug 25, 2025. The previous release was v1.8.1 on Nov 6, 2023, and before that v1.8.0 on Jul 21, 2022. That is about one release every 1-2 years, and the latest came after mid-2025. It suggests ongoing 6000 maintenance and no end-of-life freeze, which supports a slow unwind of the tail. The release content is unverified. No end-of-support or 'last version' notice appears on the page.
items.why_new: The known list covers the Illumina product, retirement and roadmap pages, but not 6000 software release dates or cadence.
